sources_read: .qc-cache/kittle-2026-10-09-r9/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx (Quality Checks row 34 / C35; Internal Quality Checks row 34 has no annotation)
evidence: Every time-varying, interactive or responsive promise in the brief is graded by a criterion that tells the judge to act, wait or resize, not to score first paint. Live/time: functional wall_added_live ('In Sian's page, without reloading, within about ten seconds M-12 disappears'), unread_and_new_messages_line (two Dev contexts, 'Within about ten seconds, without reloading, Dev's M-13 count shows 2 in both contexts', mark-unread moves the line), live_updates_keep_my_work (second context scrolled off-bottom with an open reply box and half-typed draft, then four remote changes must appear within ~10 s while draft/reply box/scroll position persist), edits_and_stale_edit (two contexts, stale save refused with reason 'still there about ten seconds later'), polish link_highlight ('still highlighted about ten seconds later') and refusal_in_place ('wait about ten seconds without touching anything'). Interaction: polish enter_sends (Shift+Enter then Enter), escape_closes (Escape on edit and reply, then reload), delete_confirm (decline then confirm), functional wall_mentions_and_links Part B (type '@', check suggestions, pick one), timer_changes (timer control 7d/off/30d with immediate disappearance). Viewport: polish transcript_phone ('At 390 by 844 ... Confirm documentElement.scrollWidth equals the viewport width'); visual phone_thread ('Gwen's matter thread at 390 by 844') with visual prompt.md:49 'resize to 1440 by 900 first, and to 390 by 844 for the phone criterion'. No theming or animation is promised by the brief, so none is needed. app_context.md gives the judge the browser_run_code_unsafe recipe for separate contexts, making the multi-context waits feasible. Feasibility on the golden: golden-run.log (hash verified) shows wall_added_live, unread_and_new_messages_line, live_updates_keep_my_work, polish_link_highlight, polish_transcript_phone and polish_refusal_in_place PASS in the scripted Playwright run (functional.cjs:716-720 sets 390x844 and asserts scrollWidth). Risk=true because no configured judge run exists for these bytes (raw-evidence-index scope: 'A full configured grading run ... absent'; functional judge.toml: 'Not yet measured against a judge run'), so whether the GLM judge actually performs the waits/resizes within the 550 s per-criterion budget is NOT EXERCISED; scripted golden is not judge behaviour. Note (adjacent, not a row-34 defect): the brief's 390 px 'without the page scrolling sideways' for the main thread is resized-and-viewed only through the visual phone_thread likert, whose anchors do not ask the judge to measure scrollWidth; a thread page that scrolls sideways at 390 but keeps content readable could still get 3-4. Strict measurement is in transcript_phone only. Coverage/precision rows should weigh this; consider adding a scrollWidth check for the thread at 390 to a polish criterion.
